newsitem.title: DENMARK: Carlsberg denies Norwegian merger plans.
newsitem.headline: Carlsberg denies Norwegian merger plans.

text.p: Danish brewer Carlsberg said on Wednesday that it was discussing possible cooperation with Norwegian beermakers Mack, Borg and Hansa but said there were no plans for the four to merge.
"If we were to merge in the form they have now it would be like a mouse merging with an elephant and it's not relevant," Carlsberg director Michael Iuul told Reuters.
He added that the Danish-based giant had no shareholding in any of the Norwegian firms.

"Carlsberg has a running dialogue with the (Norwegian) brewers on cooperation. If the three Norwegian brewers merge there would naturally be a question of increased cooperation. It may well come to something but not something that would have other than minor consequences for Carlsberg," he said.

The Norwegian business daily Dagens Naeringsliv said on Wednesday that Mack shareholders had been informed that there were several possible options ranging from a loose alliance between the four to a merger.
The brewers are seeking to compete better on the Norwegian market against local brewer Orkla and Sweden's Pripps.

Hansa's distribution deal with Coca Cola expires in October 1997, after which it is to be taken over by a Carlsberg-Coca joint venture, Coca-Cola Nordic Beverages, if the European Commission approves the project.

The Carlsberg-Coke alliance, to be based in Copenhagen, is to act as a holding company for soft-drink bottling, sales and distribution operations in Denmark, Sweden and later Norway and throughout the Nordic and Baltic regions, the Commission says.
